EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East has experienced a significant and rapid escalation in direct military confrontation between the United States and Iran over the past 24 hours. The US launched a major new wave of airstrikes against approximately 140 Iranian military targets, in response to Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran retaliated for by striking US bases and allied targets across multiple Gulf states.

IRAN
US forces, under CENTCOM, conducted a substantial new wave of strikes against Iran, hitting approximately 140 military targets on 12 July, bringing the total over the past three days to more than 300 targets. These strikes targeted missile and drone sites, naval capabilities, ammunition storage facilities, communication networks, and coastal observation posts across numerous provinces, including Khuzestan, Hormozgan, Markazi, and Sistan and Baluchestan. Specific locations affected include Omidiyeh and Mahshahr (where a water pumping station was hit, resulting in 1 killed and 4 injured), Ahvaz, Behbahan, Dezful (including Quds and Bakri Barracks, and Vahdati Airbase, leading to power cuts), Khondab (near the Arak heavy water reactor), Sirik (a telecommunications tower was struck), Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island (hit by 10-11 projectiles at military sites, with smoke seen), Jask, Abadan, Khorramshahr, Susangerd, Salehiyeh, Hamidieh, Hoveyzeh, Shadegan, and the Chazabeh border terminal. A communications sector manager, Nooh Mahdavi, was killed, and two others were injured on Farvar Island in Hormozgan. The US denies any casualties among its forces, while US officials warn of a "bigger" wave of strikes to follow.

Iran responded with missile and drone strikes targeting US bases and allied infrastructure across the region. The IRGC claimed to have struck US missile launchers (HIMARS ATACMS) at Shuaiba Port in Kuwait and the Al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar, causing explosions in Doha that injured 3 people, including 1 child. Additional Iranian strikes were reported in Bahrain (including the purported US 5th Fleet base, with multiple blasts and sirens), Jordan (where 3 ballistic missiles fell near Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, causing minor material damage), Oman (Musandam province hit by drones), and the UAE (explosions reported). Iran claims to have hit a Cyprus-flagged commercial vessel, GFS Galaxy, in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing and the ship sinking. Iran also launched a drone attack on a Kurdish-Iranian opposition camp in northern Iraq.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry condemned US strikes as "criminal aggression" and "war crimes," warning that the origins of these attacks, including countries hosting US military bases, would become legitimate targets for retaliation. Iran also declared the Strait of Hormuz closed due to "illegal" US military movements, although the US disputes this. Iranian officials Mohsen Rezaei and Javad Larijani emphasized Iran's full control over the Strait and readiness for a prolonged conflict. The country's electricity network has sustained damage, with over 2000 points hit and a 4200 MW reduction in capacity. Iranian media reported nightly rallies in support of the armed forces, and the Deputy Foreign Minister called for formal regulations for "crushing" responses to any assassination attempt against the Supreme Leader or senior officials. Iran also claimed to have thwarted a US assassination attempt against former President Trump during a visit to Turkey.

ISRAEL
The IDF conducted an airstrike on a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in Gaza City, claiming operatives were present and that the action was in response to ceasefire violations. Palestinian media reported four fatalities in this strike. The IDF also announced the elimination of two Hamas operatives in Gaza last week: Hassan Mustafa Zahir Al-Razina (on Saturday) and Mohammad Mahmoud Abd al-Mu'ti Fayyoumi (on Thursday), both accused of planning attacks against Israeli forces. In Lebanon, the IDF uncovered a Hezbollah tunnel system and underground operating room beneath the Beaufort stronghold.

On the home front, a mistaken missile warning was issued in Bnei Brak due to a cellular network technical glitch. Police cleared protests blocking the light rail in Jerusalem, with extreme Haredim demonstrating on Bar Ilan Street. Incidents of violence included a 23-year-old seriously injured in Tiberias, a 38-year-old moderately injured in Ma'ale Iron, and the murder of Benayahu Razi in Jerusalem, for which six suspects have been arrested. Emergency services also responded to a 13-year-old boy injured by a vehicle on Road 1 near Kfar Adumim and an 11-year-old girl injured in Jerusalem. The police are preparing to present findings from their investigation into the October 7th attacks to the families of fallen officers. The "special situation in the home front" was extended until July 28.

Politically, the Knesset's Constitution Committee approved a law to weaken the role of the legal advisor and the "Battle Shock Victims" law. Discussion on a law to weaken media oversight concluded quickly amid opposition criticism. The Knesset Committee is also considering a proposal to dissolve the Knesset, with elections tentatively scheduled for October 27. The Finance Committee approved 54.79 million ILS for Haredi sector economic development, and a law to freeze arrests of Haredi yeshiva students was advanced despite legal counsel objections. Shin Bet head David Zini met with opposition leader Yair Lapid. Prime Minister Netanyahu affirmed Israel's systematic efforts to crush the Iranian Axis of Evil and remove the existential threat of a nuclear Iran. Israeli officials assess that Iran is not currently seeking to attack Israel directly, fearing an escalation to high-intensity conflict, unless drawn in by the US or Iran.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF bombed a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in Gaza City, which the military stated was used to restore Hamas capabilities and violated the ceasefire. Palestinian media reported four fatalities from this strike. Two Hamas operatives, Hassan Mustafa Zahir Al-Razina and Mohammad Mahmoud Abd al-Mu'ti Fayyoumi, were killed in separate Israeli airstrikes last week. Israeli forces also responded to a report of shooting at an Israeli citizen in the Al-Mughayyir and Khirbat Abu Falah areas (Benjamin Brigade), with no casualties reported. The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire, with the transportation system nearing collapse due to war damage and fuel shortages. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers attacked independent journalists and a CNN crew in Sinjil, and burned Palestinian homes in Deir Ammar.

LEBANON
The IDF uncovered a Hezbollah tunnel system, an underground operating room, and other infrastructure beneath the historic Beaufort stronghold. Lebanese sources reported a targeted Israeli airstrike in Sar'een, South Lebanon. This period marks 20 years since Hezbollah's surprise attack that led to the abduction of Ehud Goldwasser and Eldad Regev, triggering the Second Lebanon War. The Lebanese Armed Forces have rejected any direct coordination with Israeli forces regarding proposed "pilot zones" in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iran launched a drone attack targeting a Kurdish-Iranian opposition camp in northern Iraq, with explosions reported in Sulaymaniyah province. The Islamic Resistance in Iraq issued a statement opposing the Iraqi government delegation's visit to Washington, warning against economic dependence on the US and the continued presence of US forces in Iraq. Reports also indicate explosions at a US base on the Kuwait-Iraq border, suggesting potential spillover effects from the wider regional conflict. Luminous objects were observed in the sky over Arbil in the Kurdistan region.

GULF STATES
**Kuwait:** The Ministry of Defense confirmed that three land border posts in northern Kuwait were attacked, and an offshore drilling platform owned by the Kuwait Oil Company was hit by a drone, injuring one worker and causing material damage. Kuwait condemned the Iranian attacks as a "dangerous escalation," and its Army Chief of Staff affirmed the armed forces are on full readiness. Iranian sources claimed 3 US soldiers were killed in Kuwaiti-based HIMARS attacks, but CENTCOM explicitly denied any US casualties.
**Qatar:** Former Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani passed away at age 74, prompting four days of mourning. His death led to condolences from Iranian President Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Araghchi. Al-Udeid Air Base was reportedly attacked by the IRGC, and explosions in Doha injured 3 people from missile debris. Qatar has temporarily halted tanker movements due to the security situation.
**Bahrain:** Multiple explosions and sirens were reported, with Iranian sources claiming a US 5th Fleet base was hit.
**UAE:** Explosions were reported. Iran issued a warning to citizens in Kuwait, Bahrain, and the UAE to evacuate military zones.
**Oman:** The Musandam province was attacked by drones, leading Oman to summon the Iranian ambassador to protest the incidents.
**Saudi Arabia:** Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan engaged in diplomatic calls with counterparts in Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, and Jordan, emphasizing the need for diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions.
**Strait of Hormuz:** Both the US and Iran maintain conflicting positions on its status. Iran (IRGC and Persian Gulf Strait Authority) declared it closed or under "Iranian arrangements," while US CENTCOM and President Trump insist it remains open for legal international shipping. CENTCOM stated that 800 commercial vessels and 400 million barrels of crude oil have transited the Strait safely since May, partly facilitated by US forces, and 20 commercial vessels transited in coordination with the US military in the last 24 hours. US F-35A fighter jets were seen refueling over the Middle East, and a US early warning aircraft took off from Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, demonstrating a heightened US military posture.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  US CENTCOM launched a major new wave of strikes against Iran, hitting approximately 140 military targets on 12 July across multiple provinces, bringing the three-day total to over 300 targets, including missile sites, air defense systems, and naval capabilities.
2.  Iran conducted retaliatory missile and drone strikes against US military bases and allied targets in Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman, and the UAE.
3.  The Strait of Hormuz is a critical flashpoint; Iran declared it closed or under its control, while the US asserts freedom of navigation, with both sides actively engaged in military actions and asserting their authority over the waterway.
4.  Casualties reported include 1 Iranian communications manager killed and 2 injured in Hormozgan, 1 killed and 4 injured in Mahshahr/Omidiyeh, 1 Kuwaiti worker injured on an offshore platform, and 3 people (including 1 child) injured in Qatar from missile debris. Iranian claims of 3 US soldiers killed in Kuwait were denied by CENTCOM.
5.  The IDF launched airstrikes against a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in Gaza City, which reportedly killed 4 Palestinians, and eliminated two Hamas operatives in separate strikes last week.
6.  US Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Israel and a prominent hawk on Iran, died at age 71 after a "sudden and brief illness."
7.  Iran claimed to have thwarted a US assassination attempt on former President Trump during his visit to Turkey, based on foreign intelligence.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high, with direct US-Iran military engagement intensifying significantly. Both sides have demonstrated a willingness to conduct widespread strikes beyond previous patterns, affecting multiple regional actors. The Strait of Hormuz remains an active flashpoint, with conflicting claims of control and ongoing military presence. Other active flashpoints include southern and central Iranian provinces, US bases and allied territories in Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman, and the UAE, as well as northern Iraq. The US appears to have established that attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz are a red line, while Iran views US strikes on its territory as "criminal aggression" justifying retaliation against the origin points of such attacks, including countries hosting US bases. Both US and Iranian forces are on high alert, actively engaged in offensive and defensive operations, and prepared for further confrontation.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** has reiterated its commitment to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with President Trump authorizing new strikes and stating Iran broke an earlier deal. **Kuwait** condemned Iranian attacks as a "dangerous escalation" and affirmed military readiness. **Qatar** halted tanker movements and received condolences from Iran's leadership for the passing of its former Emir. **Oman** summoned the Iranian ambassador in protest of drone attacks. **Saudi Arabia's** Foreign Minister engaged in diplomatic discussions with regional counterparts to emphasize de-escalation efforts. The **UN Secretary-General** expressed deep concern over the escalation, calling for diplomacy and warning of "catastrophic consequences." **Pakistan** urged restraint and commitment to dialogue. **Yemen** reaffirmed full support for Iran, warning of negative impacts on the global economy. The **Iraqi Islamic Resistance** condemned the Iraqi government's engagement with the US, citing US military presence and economic dominance. **Ukraine** conducted extensive drone attacks on Russian vessels and oil infrastructure, while a New York Times report highlighted Tokyo as a new hub for Russian intelligence operations aimed at circumventing sanctions.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant ambiguity exists regarding the status of **Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei**. Conflicting reports from Naya and PressTV implying his martyrdom contradict other PressTV and Iranian sources that refer to him in the present tense or in contexts suggesting he is alive. For this briefing, it is assumed he is not deceased, and "martyred leader" refers to a different individual, possibly a propaganda term.

There are **contradictory reports on US casualties in Kuwait**; Iranian sources claim 3 US soldiers were killed, while US CENTCOM explicitly denies any US casualties. The **status of the Strait of Hormuz** remains contested, with Iran declaring it closed/under its control and the US asserting it is open for international navigation. While Iran claimed to thwart an assassination attempt on President Trump in Turkey, independent verification of the specific details and Iranian intent is lacking. The extent of **damage to military and civilian infrastructure** in Iran and US/Gulf bases from the widespread strikes is still being assessed, with full independent verification pending. Propaganda indicators are evident in Iranian media's celebratory reporting on the death of US Senator Lindsey Graham and in both US and Iranian statements framing their actions for internal and external audiences.
